summary: CeladonHealth ingestion timeouts trigger model-unavailable fallbacks and fanout amplification during nightly billing window
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-14T12:45Z CeladonHealth observed client requests intermittently timing out at the ingestion gateway. The router returned model-unavailable fallbacks which caused a cascade of retries and amplified fanout across Dedicated pools. Impact: CeladonHealth reported a ~95% increase in failed completions and a 3x spike in token billing during the nightly billing reconciliation window. Customer impact: degraded product experience for end users during batch reconciliation; potential overage billing exposure.

Immediate ask from customer: stop the amplification, restore stable routing to pinned model version, and confirm billing exposure scope.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send parallel batch ingestion requests (10k req/min) to /v1/completions with client header X-Celadon-Batch: true
2) Observe ingestion-gateway logs for repeated 504/timeout responses between 12:30-13:00 UTC
3) Watch router decisions (trace_id header) showing fallback to model variant 'redwood-opt-8k-fallback'
4) Monitor Dedicated pool metrics for sudden increase in connection count and retry rates
logs: 2026-03-14T12:47:02Z ingestion-gateway ERROR request_id=abc123 timeout waiting for backend (500ms) route=celadon-v1
2026-03-14T12:47:03Z serving-runtime WARN pool=dedicated-west connection_count=482 spike_from=120 backpressure=true
comments: 2026-03-14T13:02Z | Diego Martinez (SRE): Investigating ingestion gateway timeouts. Early signal shows backend connection queue surge; rate limiter may be misconfigured for batch header. No mitigation yet.

2026-03-14T13:15Z | Samantha Lee (Support, on call): Customer reporting stream truncation and retried completions. Escalated to Enterprise CS. Customer asking for immediate routing pin to the stable variant.

2026-03-14T13:34Z | Priya Nair (Serving): Observed kernel selection thrash on redwood-opt-8k-fallback during long sequences; metrics show heavy KV cache churn. Suggest temporary routing to llama-3-13b-q4 which has stable qkv profile.

2026-03-14T13:50Z | Diego Martinez (SRE): Applied emergency router override to pin CeladonHealth to llama-3-13b-q4 for the next 30m. Early telemetry indicates error rate falling back to baseline. Noting potential cost delta.
2026-03-15T09:12Z | Billing (Ana Torres): Initial estimate that customer saw ~+1.8x token bill in affected window; flagged for reconciliation and potential credit.

2026-03-16T11:05Z | Diego Martinez (SRE): Root cause identified as simultaneous increase in client-side parallelism plus a mis-evaluated admission-control threshold in ingestion-gateway v1.4.2; rollout of 1.4.3 patch contains fix and adjusted admission thresholds.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Batch header (X-Celadon-Batch) caused unexpected head-of-line blocking in ingestion-gateway due to an old per-client concurrency cap algorithm. Evidence: elevated queue times for requests containing the batch header and corresponding 504s.

Hypothesis 2: Router fallback amplified requests because fallback variant 'redwood-opt-8k-fallback' triggered heavier KV recompute and longer kernel latencies, causing downstream backpressure and more timeouts. Evidence: serving-runtime traces show 2-3x higher p95 kernel time for fallback variant.

Telemetry checked: ingestion-gateway queue_len, router_fallback_rate, serving-runtime p95/p99 latency, dedicated pool connection_count, billing token rate. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/ingestion-gateway-overview and https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/model-latency

Reproduction attempts in staging with replayed Celadon traffic reproduced timeout pattern only when admission-control threshold was set to legacy value. With updated threshold, ingestion queue stabilized.

Related config: admission_control.concurrency_per_client was 250 in v1.4.2; tuned to 80 in v1.4.3. Also adjusted router fallback penalty to reduce immediate fallbacks during transient backend pressure.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-14T13:50Z): emergency router override to pin CeladonHealth traffic to llama-3-13b-q4; ingestion-gateway concurrency cap reduced for enterprise clients to prevent queue storms.

Permanent fix (deployed 2026-03-15T02:10Z): ingestion-gateway v1.4.3 rolled out to us-west-2 with tuned admission-control, improved backpressure signaling, and a fix to the batch header handling logic. Router fallback penalty adjusted to prevent immediate amplification loops.
Customer communication: Notified CeladonHealth on 2026-03-14 at 14:15Z with interim action and 2026-03-15 at 10:00Z with full resolution and billing reconciliation plan.
Billing remediation: Billing team issued a provisional credit for the affected window; final reconciliation pending after full audit (owner: Ana Torres).
follow_up_actions: 1) Post-incident runbook update: add explicit guidance for admission-control tuning for large batch headers and enterprise customers (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-03-22).

2) Router policy change: introduce soft-fallback delay and jitter to avoid synchronous fallback amplification (owner: Diego Martinez, PR in progress https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/452).
3) Customer-facing: schedule a technical review with CeladonHealth to review best practices for batch ingestion and concurrency (owner: Samantha Lee, scheduled 2026-03-18).
4) Billing: complete audit of token delta and finalize credit by 2026-03-20 (owner: Ana Torres).
5) Monitoring: add synthetic test for batch-header heavy workload to alert at 2x baseline queue length (owner: Observability team).
